current.text: Washington acquired Ayton from the Lakers for Jaden Hardy and second-round picks. He is the backup big man behind Alex Sarr and Anthony Davis and comes off the bench.
Washington lacks depth at center behind Sarr and Davis.
Experts say he is no longer the player he was in Phoenix.
Davis's health is a question, so Ayton could get 30-minute roles at times when Davis is out.
His FG% jump last season may have been helped by playing with Luka. He now plays with Trae Young, and the expert says not to assume a big FG% drop.
One expert is about 80% sure Washington keeps Davis, but a Davis trade cannot be ruled out. If Davis is traded, Sarr starts at center.
Washington is trying to compete and expects to be near .500 and in the play-in mix, so the late-season resting and minutes cuts of past years should not return.

durable.text: He is an efficient finisher whose FG% helps, but on low shot volume. Assists and steals are weak.
